text: Repeated threats or intimidation from the accused party often precede acute anxiety and hypervigilance in victims.
Delays in investigation or trial proceedings are strongly associated with prolonged psychological distress and helplessness.
Social ostracism and community isolation after a complaint can manifest as withdrawal, reduced check-in frequency, and hopeless language.
Economic hardship following a complaint, such as job loss or lost wages, compounds stress and can indicate elevated risk when combined with other signals.
Direct mention of safety threats or being followed should always be treated as a high-priority escalation signal.
Sleep disturbance and repeated mentions of exhaustion are common early indicators of deteriorating mental health in this population.
